item.title: The Dimension Conjecture for Hypersurfaces Is True
item.description: arXiv:2611.10314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dimension conjecture in CR geometry is proved for an arbitrary real-analytic hypersurface. More precisely, we prove that the dimension of the algebra of infinitesimal holomorphic automorphisms of a germ of a holomorphically nondegenerate hypersurface in $\mathbb{C}^N$ in this class does not exceed $N^2+2N$. This number is exactly the corresponding dimension for any nondegenerate hyperquadric in the same ambient space. Moreover, equality holds if and only if the germ is equivalent to a hyperquadric.
item.dc:creator: M. A. Stepanova

item.title: A Zero-Free Sum of Cauchy Kernels with Positive Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.10492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a zero-free meromorphic function \[ f(z)=\sum_n\frac{c_n}{z-a_n},\qquad c_n>0,\qquad |a_n|\to\infty,\qquad \sum_{a_n\ne0}\frac{c_n}{|a_n|}<\infty, \] thereby disproving the Clunie--Eremenko--Rossi conjecture. The construction starts from a product of two rotated Airy functions. The zeros of this product are shifted simultaneously so that all residues of $f$ are positive. The poles lie on the rays $e^{\pm i\pi/3}[0,\infty)$. The resulting function has order and lower order $3/2$, and the sum of its residues in the disc $|z|\le r$ is asymptotic to $\frac{4}{3\pi}r^{3/4}$.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Shemyakov

item.title: Holomorphic interpolation and the Levi problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.10807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On a nonsingular locally Stein Riemann domain over a Stein space, we prove that holomorphic forms of top degree interpolate jets of any fixed order on every closed discrete set finite over the base. For unramified domains, this yields jet interpolation by holomorphic functions, answering a question of Col\c{t}oiu and Joi\c{t}a for nonsingular sources. More generally, we establish a twisted interpolation theorem over weakly pseudoconvex spaces admitting injective holomorphic immersions into projective space. We also give negative answers to the Levi problem over singular Stein spaces: the Coeur\'e-Loeb space yields a non-Stein locally Stein unramified Riemann domain over a normal Stein threefold, and a related construction gives a relatively compact, non-Stein locally Stein open subset of a normal Stein fourfold. Finally, the punctured anticanonical bundle of Fornaess' ramified surface is a holomorphically separable increasing union of Stein manifolds that is not Stein, answering a question of Vigna Suria.
item.dc:creator: Yuta Kusakabe, Takeo Ohsawa

item.title: Holomorphic Isometric Embeddings of the Unit Disk into the Symmetrized Bidisk
item.description: arXiv:2611.10983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a complete characterization of the holomorphic isometric embeddings $F:(\mathbb{D},k\,ds^2)\rightarrow (\mathbb{G}_2,ds^2)$ of the unit disk into the symmetrized bidisk with respect to the Bergman metric up to a scalar constant. We show that the isometric constant $k$ can take only the values $k=1$ and $k=3$. For $k=3$, we prove that $(2z,z^2)$ is the unique isometry up to a reparametrization. For $k=1$, we construct an isometric embedding which intersects the royal variety at a single point and does not admit a holomorphic lift to the bidisk via the symmetrization map. We further show that this isometric embedding is unique up to reparametrizations. Finally, none of the isometries are totally geodesic.
item.dc:creator: Aakanksha Jain

item.title: Bott--Chern and Aeppli Cohomology of toroidal groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.11184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups of theta toroidal groups in arbitrary dimensions, obtaining explicit dimension formulas and bases in all bidegrees. For general toroidal groups, we determine the Hausdorff reductions of these cohomology groups and show that they coincide with those of theta toroidal groups. We also compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups themselves in certain specific bidegrees, without passing to their Hausdorff reductions.
item.dc:creator: Xiaojun Wu

item.title: Hausdorff Dimension of Escaping Sets of Transcendental Entire Functions in the Speiser Class
item.description: arXiv:2611.11385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every $d\in[1,2]$, we construct a transcendental entire function $f$ whose finite singular value is contained in $\{-1,0,1\}$ and whose escaping set has Hausdorff dimension $d$. For $d<2$, the construction combines spiral corridors with quasiconformal folding. A narrowing Archimedean spiral gives dimension one, while a logarithmic spiral with adjustable width gives intermediate dimensions. The endpoint $d=2$ is realized by the exponential map. This gives an affirmative answer to a question of Bishop posed in 2018.
item.dc:creator: Yuming Fu, Weiwei Su

item.title: Smooth limits of compact Kahler manifolds with vanishing first Chern class
item.description: arXiv:2611.11925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\pi\colon X\to\Delta$ be a proper holomorphic submersion from a smooth complex manifold onto the unit disc. Suppose that for every $t\in\Delta^*$ the fiber $X_t$ is a compact Kahler manifold whose real first Chern class vanishes. We prove that the central fiber X_0 belongs to Fujiki's class $\cC$, that is, X_0 is bimeromorphic to a compact Kahler manifold.
item.dc:creator: Mu-Lin Li

item.title: Branch points and natural boundaries of Poincar\'e functions and of solutions of nonlinear functional differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.12213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the singularity structure of the analytic continuation of solutions to the equation $g(\lambda w)=R(g(w))$, where $|\lambda|<1$ and $R$ is a rational function. We show that the analytic solution \(g\) near zero is branched, and that its analytic continuation yields an infinite-sheeted Riemann surface with various patterns of branch points. In one specific pattern, some branch points are delayed: they appear only when the analytic continuation reaches a particular Riemann sheet. Using this functional-equation framework, we extend the study to first-order nonlinear functional differential equations. We show that the continuation of certain special solutions near an attracting fixed point yields either single-valued or multivalued functions, with the unit circle as a natural boundary on every sheet.
item.dc:creator: Techheang Meng

item.title: Unique continuation property for $\bar\partial$ with $L^{2n}$ potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.12449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the sharp unique continuation property for the Cauchy--Riemann operator $\bar{\partial}$ in higher dimensions. Let $0\in\Omega \subset \C^n$ be a domain. Suppose $u \in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,2}(\Omega; \C^N)$ satisfies the differential inequality \[ |\bar{\partial} u| \leq V |u| \quad \text{a.e.~on } \Omega \] with $V \in L_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2n}(\Omega)$. If $u$ is $L^2$ flat at the origin, then $u \equiv 0$ on $\Omega$.
item.dc:creator: Guokuan Shao, Ziming Shi, Jujie Wu

item.title: On the entire solutions of Schr\"{o}der iteration functions of first and second kind
item.description: arXiv:2611.12593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S_{f,n}$ and $K_{f,n}$ denote Schr\"oder's methods of the first and second kind with given order $ n $ ($\geq 2 $) applied to an entire function $ f $. This article investigates the existence of the entire solutions $f$ whenever $ S_{f,n} $ and $ K_{f,n} $ are rational. Utilizing the Nevanlinna theory, we obtain the general form of entire solutions for such equations. It is proved that either of $ S_{f,n} $ and $ K_{f,n} $ is a non-identity rational map if and only if $f = p e^{q}$, for some polynomials $p$ and $q$. Additionally, we provide one recurrence relation of $K_{f,n}$ depending only upon $K_{f,n-1}$.
item.dc:creator: Subhasis Ghora, Gang Liu, Soumen Pal, Saminathan Ponnusamy

item.title: A proof of the Erd\H{o}s-Herzog-Piranian lemniscate conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.12830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n\geq 1$. In 1958, Erd\H{o}s, Herzog, and Piranian conjectured that the length of the lemniscate $\{z\in\mathbb C:|p(z)|=1\}$ is maximized by $p(z)=z^n-1$. We prove this conjecture in every degree and show that equality holds precisely for $p(z)=(z-z_0)^n-e^{i\theta}$, where $z_0\in\mathbb C$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$. The proof uses M\"obius variations of the critical values and estimates for the inverse branches of $p$, supplemented by rigorous computer-assisted estimates in a finite range of degrees.
item.dc:creator: Teng Zhang

item.title: An Alternative Proof of the SPR Synthesis Theorem for Polynomial Segments of Arbitrary Order
item.description: arXiv:2611.09940v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For any positive integer n and any two monic real Hurwitz polynomials of degree n, every convex combination of the two is Hurwitz stable if and only if there exists a common numerator of degree n that makes both endpoint transfer functions strictly positive real. We give a unified proof based on convex separation, contact interpolation, and analytic properties of weakly positive real functions.
item.dc:creator: Zhengtai Xiong, Tiancheng Xu, Xiang Ji, Guowei Dou, Long Wang, Wensheng Yu

item.title: Metric nefness of direct image sheaves under weakly semi-stable K\"ahler morphisms
item.description: arXiv:2611.10391v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the nefness of the direct image sheaves of relative adjoint bundles under weakly semi-stable K\"ahler morphisms between complex spaces. We show that the direct image sheaves are locally free and that their tautological line bundles are metrically nef, strengthening the previously known results on torsion-freeness and certain weak positivity.
item.dc:creator: Osamu Fujino, Shigeharu Takayama

item.title: Schauder exponential basis which is not Riesz
item.description: arXiv:2611.10799v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that there exists a Schauder basis $\{e^{i \lambda_n t}\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with real frequencies in $L^2(-\pi,\pi)$ which is not a Riesz basis.
item.dc:creator: Andrei V. Semenov

item.title: The moduli stack of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type
item.description: arXiv:2611.10879v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The goal of this article is the classification of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type over a compact complex manifold $X$. More precisely, let $E$ be a fixed holomorphic vector bundle over $X$ and $\mathcal{E}$ the associated locally free sheaf. We will assume that there exists an effective divisor $D$ on $X$ such that $H^1(X,\mathcal{E}(D))=0$. This condition is always satisfied when $X$ is a projective complex manifold. We define in a natural way the moduli stack of affine bundles on $X$ whose linearisation is isomorphic to $E$, and we prove that this moduli stack is isomorphic to the quotient stack $\big[H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D)_D)/H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D))\ltimes \mathrm{Aut}(E)\big]$ of the complex vector space $H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D)_D)$ by the semi-direct product of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(E)$ (which is always an affine algebraic group) by the complex vector space $H^0(X,{\cal E}(D))$. Our isomorphism is obtained by constructing explicitly comparison functors $\mathscr{A}$, $\mathscr{T}$ between the two stacks and explicit natural isomorphisms $\mathscr{A}\circ\mathscr{T}\stackrel{\simeq}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{id}$, $\mathrm{id} \stackrel{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\mathscr{T}\circ\mathscr{A}$.
item.dc:creator: Naoufal Bouchareb, Andrei Teleman

item.title: Pluriclosed flow on K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.11614v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the maximal existence conjecture for pluriclosed flow on K\"ahler backgrounds. This leads to a priori generalizations of the Aubin-Yau and Calabi-Yau theorems, and resolves the question of connectedness of generalized K\"ahler structures on Calabi-Yau backgrounds.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Streets

item.title: Spectral Stability, Fatou Basin Contraction, and Machine-Checked Multipliers in Holomorphic Extensions of Generalized Syracuse Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.11641v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We embed the Syracuse operator $T(n) = n/2$ (even $n$), $T(n) = (3n+1)/2$ (odd $n$) and the Collatz map $C(n)$ into $\mathbb{C}$ via entire functions of exponential type $\pi$: $f(z) = \frac{1}{4}(1 + 4z - (1 + 2z)\cos(\pi z))$ and $F(z) = \frac{1}{4}(2 + 7z - (2 + 5z)\cos(\pi z))$. We prove five results: (1) every integer periodic cycle $C \subset \mathbb{N}^+$ of $T$ is a strictly attracting Fatou cycle of $f$ with multiplier $\mu_f(C) = 3^{N_{\mathrm{odd}}}/2^N = \prod_{n \in C\text{ odd}} \frac{3n}{3n+1} \in (0,1)$, and $\mu_f(O_{1,2}) = \mu_F(O_{1,4,2}) = 3/4 < 1$; (2) on the Fatou basin $B(O_{1,2})$, $g = f^{\circ 2}$ conjugates to $\Phi_j(g(z)) = \frac{3}{4}\Phi_j(z)$ with Koenigs Taylor jets $c_2(1) = -\frac{13}{2}\pi^2$ and $d_2(2) = -\frac{9}{2}\pi^2$; (3) the Schwarzian derivative is strictly negative on $\mathbb{Z}$ ($S(f)(n) \le 3\pi^2 - \frac{3}{8}\pi^4 \approx -6.9196 < 0$), and a repelling Julia 2-cycle $O_{\mathrm{rep}} \subset J(f)$ ($\mu \approx 1.2148 > 1$) isolates $B(O_{1,2})$; (4) on $(\mathbb{Z}_2, \mu_{\mathrm{Haar}})$, the 2-adic Lyapunov exponent $\lambda_{\mathrm{Haar}} = \frac{1}{2}\ln(3/4) \approx -0.143841 < 0$ equals $\frac{1}{2}\ln|\mu_f(O_{1,2})|$; and (5) we certify 20 theorems in Lean 4 (anc/CollatzAttractor.lean, 0 sorry). These results establish local Fatou invariants and 2-adic ergodic averages for $f(z)$, leaving open whether every $n_0 \in \mathbb{N}^+$ lies in $\bigcup_{k \ge 0} f^{-k}(B(O_{1,2}))$.
item.dc:creator: Volkan Da\u{g}l{\i}, Zerrin Da\u{g}l{\i}, Da\u{g}han Da\u{g}l{\i}, Emrah Yurtseven, Murat Emre \"Ozkaya

item.title: Compact branch sets and injectivity of proper branched coverings
item.description: arXiv:2611.11844v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we show that a proper continuous open discrete map from the open unit ball $B^n$ onto a domain in $\R^n$ with $n\geq5$ is a homeomorphism whenever its branch set is compact. This answers Vuorinen's question affirmatively in every dimension $n\ge5.$ In dimension four, we also show that, under the additional assumption of quasiregularity, the map is a quasiconformal homeomorphism. Together with the three-dimensional theorem of Kauranen, Luisto and Tengvall, these results answer the quasiregular question posed as Problem~7.66 in the collections of Barth--Brannan--Hayman and Hayman--Lingham in every dimension $n\ge3$.
item.dc:creator: Deguang Zhong

item.title: Lower bound of the Calabi functional and non-Archimedean K-energy
item.description: arXiv:2611.11938v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove Donaldson's conjecture which describes the infimum of the Calabi functional by the normalized non-Archimedean K-energy. The proof makes use of proximal equation for the K-energy. To obtain approximate smooth solutions, a continuity path of prescribed scalar curvature equation is coupled with a version of Chen's $\e$-subgeodesic. It does not require a global smooth solution to the Calabi flow.
item.dc:creator: Tomoyuki Hisamoto

item.title: Branched real projective structures on surfaces, cyclic Higgs Bundles and Anosov representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.12101v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use the theory of $3$-cyclic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$-Higgs bundles to study real branched projective structures on compact surfaces recently introduced by the authors. After fixing a Riemann surface structure on $S$, the Higgs bundle approach allows us, on the one hand, to construct branched structures with prescribed branching data and, on the other hand, to introduce new classes of such structures. The latter are directly related to singular hyperbolic affine spheres and carry a Blaschke metric with conical singularities. In the final part of the paper, using different methods, we prove that every Anosov surface group representation into $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$ is either Hitchin or belongs to the Barbot component. As a by-product, we obtain that some of the representations associated with the branched structures constructed above are not Anosov.
item.dc:creator: Gianluca Faraco, Nicholas Rungi

item.title: Singularities in leaf closures on complex surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.12402v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a geometric and dynamical criterion excluding minimal sets contained in the regular locus of a holomorphic foliation on a compact complex surface. In particular, we prove that every Jouanolou foliation of degree at least two has no exceptional minimal set. We also give an explicit lower bound, growing linearly with the degree, for the number of singularities in every regular leaf closure of a Jouanolou foliation. This bound persists under small perturbations, as does the existence of a nonempty open saturated set whose leaves accumulate at all singularities. Under finite pullback unramified over the singular set, the bound is multiplied by the degree of the normalised component over the base leaf. Together with a general persistence theorem, this yields nonempty analytic open sets of foliations on every smooth projective surface with arbitrarily large uniform lower bounds on the number of singularities in their regular leaf closures. On double-plane K3 surfaces, we obtain foliations with ample canonical bundle and explicitly describe and count their singularities.
item.dc:creator: Mauricio Corr\^ea, Fernando Reis

item.title: The Paley--Wiener excess and a local law for the ${\rm Sine}_\beta$ process
item.description: arXiv:2611.12602v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The main result of this paper is the proof that the Paley--Wiener excess of the ${\rm Sine}_\beta$ process almost surely equals $\lfloor \sqrt{2/\beta}\rfloor$ for all $\beta>0$. We also derive the loop equations for the resolvent of the ${\rm Sine}_\beta$ point process and use them to obtain accurate bounds on the moments of the associated Stieltjes transform.
item.dc:creator: Paul Bourgade, Mikhail Sodin, Ofer Zeitouni

item.title: Global zero distribution and pluripolar exceptional cones for complex linear differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.12670v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the zeros of solutions of complex linear differential equations of arbitrary order $n\ge2$ with exponential-sum coefficients. Using the initial-value space $\mathbb{C}^n$ to parametrize the solutions, we show that solutions with initial vectors outside a complete pluripolar cone of Lebesgue measure zero share an explicit common leading term for the global zero count and a common joint limit in radius and angle. The rescaled radial distance from the disk boundary has an exponential limiting distribution, while the rescaled angular deviations from each main ray are Gaussian. Inspired by logarithmic tracts in the Eremenko-Lyubich class $\mathcal{B}$, we pull exterior sectors back conformally to countably many curvilinear strips extending in finitely many directions and obtain zero-counting asymptotics in each strip, although the coefficients may lie outside this class. Moreover, the asymptotic formula for the global zero count and the joint limit in radius and angle persist under arbitrary entire perturbations of strictly smaller weighted exponential type.
item.dc:creator: Xing-Yu Li

item.title: The Szeg\H{o} log-term and local rigidity of K\"ahler--Einstein polarizations of compact Hermitian symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.12708v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove local rigidity of the vanishing Szeg\H{o} log-term for integral K\"ahler--Einstein polarizations of a product of irreducible compact Hermitian symmetric spaces. Near the invariant metric, vanishing of the log-term forces the K\"ahler form to lie in its biholomorphic orbit. The argument combines the first variation of the Kempf distortion function with a central-positioning procedure, reducing rigidity to polynomiality of spectral multipliers of the Laplace operator and the Berezin transform. For integral K\"ahler--Einstein polarizations, a common-pole obstruction then rules out all infinitesimal deformations transverse to the automorphism orbit.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Loi, Matteo Palmieri, Fabio Zuddas

item.title: The Bruce-Roberts number of holomorphic 1-forms along complex analytic varieties
item.description: arXiv:2409.01237v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the notion of the \textit{Bruce--Roberts number} for holomorphic 1-forms relative to complex analytic varieties. Our main result shows that the Bruce--Roberts number of a 1-form $\omega$ relative to a complex analytic hypersurface $X$ with an isolated singularity can be expressed in terms of the \textit{Gom\'ez-Mont--Seade--Verjovsky index} of $\omega$ along $X$, the \textit{Milnor number} of $\omega$ and the \textit{Tjurina number} of $X$. This result allows us to recover known formulas for the Bruce--Roberts number of a holomorphic function along $X$ and to establish connections between this number, the radial index, and the local Euler obstruction of $\omega$ along $X$. Moreover, we present applications to both global and local holomorphic foliations in complex dimension two.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Barbosa, Arturo Fern\'andez-P\'erez, V\'ictor Le\'on

item.title: On $q$-real and $q$-complex numbers
item.description: arXiv:2508.08440v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In arXiv:1812.00170 and arXiv:1908.04365, Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko introduced $q$-rational numbers $[x]_q$, rational functions specializing to $x$ at $q=1$, and their extension to $q$-real numbers, Laurent series agreeing with $[x]_q$ for rational $x$. It was conjectured in arXiv:2102.00891 that for every real $x>1$, $[x]_q$ has positive radius of convergence, with optimal common radius $R_*=(3-\sqrt{5})/2$, attained at the golden ratio. We prove that $[x]_q$ converges to a nonvanishing holomorphic function for every real $x>1$ and $|q|<3-2\sqrt{2}$. The proof gives an expansion of $1/[x]_q$ as a $q$-adically convergent series of rational functions, converging absolutely and locally uniformly on an explicit region. It also defines a positive analytic function for $q\in(-R_*,1)$. Using arXiv:2405.15970, we further obtain convergence for $|q|<2-\sqrt{3}$. We compute $[x]_q$ explicitly for some transcendental $x$, including ${\rm cotan}(1)$ and $e$. We also establish sharp inequalities for numerators and denominators of $q$-rationals when $|q|=1$ and determine the closure of the set of $[x]_q$ when such $q$ is not a root of unity. Next, we show that coefficientwise reduction modulo every $m\ge2$ is injective on the Cantor line (the extended real line with doubled up rationals and the Cantor set topology); for $m=2$, it identifies the Cantor line with $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_2((q)))$. We describe the inverse map, extend rationality results modulo every prime, characterize quadratic series over $\mathbb F_2(q)$ corresponding to quadratic irrationals, derive criteria for eventual parity of coefficients, and compute the real numbers corresponding to $1+q^n$. Finally, we propose a definition of $q$-complex number $[\tau]_q$, a meromorphic function in $\tau\in\mathbb C_+$ expressed via hypergeometric functions evaluated at modular functions of $\tau$.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Etingof

item.title: A Hadamard Formula for Equilibrium Envelopes under Parallel Deformation
item.description: arXiv:2607.17187v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(X,\omega_0)$ be a compact K\"ahler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $U\Subset X$ have $C^{3,1}$ uniformly strongly pseudoconvex boundary. Consider the signed parallel family $U_t=\{\rho<t\}$, where $\rho$ is a defining function agreeing near $\partial U$ with the signed distance, negative in $U$. Let $u_t$ be the equilibrium envelope with zero obstacle on $X\setminus U_t$, and write $\Sigma_t=\partial U_t$, with outward unit normal $\nu_t$. We prove that the normalized Monge--Amp\`ere energy $e(t)=E_{\omega_0}(u_t)$ belongs to $C^{1,1/2}([-\tau,\tau])$ for some $\tau>0$ and satisfies the Hadamard formula $$ e'(t)=\frac{1}{n+1}\int_{\Sigma_t}\left(-\partial_{\nu_t}u_t\right)^2 d\sigma_{\rho,t}^{\mathrm{tot}}, |t|<\tau. $$ Here $d\sigma_{\rho,t}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the interior outward Anzellotti trace of $$ \frac{1}{V} d^c\rho\wedge \sum_{p=0}^{n-1}(p+1) \omega_{u_t}^{p}\wedge\omega_0^{n-1-p}, V=\int_X\omega_0^n, \omega_{u_t}=\omega_0+dd^c u_t. $$ This measure is positive and uniformly comparable to the induced surface measure. The proof combines uniform $C^{1,1}$ estimates up to the boundary from the interior with $1/2$-H\"older stability of the normal derivatives under the normal-flow identifications. We identify the boundary part of the normalized Monge--Amp\`ere measure with the negative outward trace of a divergence-measure flux current. The one-sided weak-* limits of the mixed Bedford--Taylor boundary measures yield the weighted total flux appearing in the variation formula.
item.dc:creator: Ziyu Li

item.title: Geometric folding and maximal asymptotic variance
item.description: arXiv:2611.09697v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Based on the recent breakthroughs by OpenAI and consequently by Binder-Ivrii-Prause-Smirnov, we develop a finite-scale folding method for the nonlinearity of a schlicht function, based on a signed critical-point count for superharmonic potentials and a quantitative target cutoff. Furthermore, we use a cylindrical root transform to reduce the logarithmic cost of access to the point at infinity. Combined with a Littlewood-Paley formula as well as dilation, the method yields the maximal asymptotic variance bound $\Sigma_{\max}^2\le1$ for the unrestricted schlicht class of normalized univalent functions.
item.dc:creator: Haakan Hedenmalm

item.title: A formula for the edge density $\sqrt{n}$-correction for two-dimensional Coulomb systems
item.description: arXiv:2510.16945v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In connection with recent work on smallest gaps, C. Charlier proves that the 1-point function of a suitable planar Coulomb system $\{z_j\}_1^n$, in the determinantal case with respect to an external potential $Q(z)$, admits the expansion, as $n\to\infty$, $$R_n\bigg(z_0+\frac t {\sqrt{2n\partial\bar{\partial} Q(z_0)}}\nu(z_0)\bigg)=n\partial\bar{\partial} Q(z_0)\frac {\operatorname{erfc} t}2+\sqrt{n\partial\bar{\partial} Q(z_0)}\,C(z_0;t)+\mathcal{O}(\log^6 n).$$ Here $t$ is a real parameter, $z_0$ is a regular boundary point of the (connected) Coulomb droplet and $\nu(z_0)$ is the outwards unit normal; the coefficient $C(z_0;t)$ has an apriori structure depending on a number of parameters. In this note we identify the parameters and obtain a formula for $C(z_0;t)$ in potential theoretic and geometric terms. Our formula holds for a large class of potentials such that the droplet is connected with smooth boundary. Our derivation uses the well known expectation of fluctuations formula.
item.dc:creator: Yacin Ameur

item.title: A universal model for the bifurcations of asymptotic values
item.description: arXiv:2603.15466v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a universal model for the bifurcation of asymptotic values, based on the notion of tangent-like maps and families thereof. In analogy with polynomials and polynomial-like maps, we prove that every tangent-like map can be associated to a member of the model family. In particular, the filled Julia sets of tangent-like maps are quasiconformally homeomorphic to the ones for the model family. Likewise, the bifurcation locus of a family of tangent-like maps is homeomorphic to the boundary of the {\em Tandelbrot set} $\mathcal T$, the bifurcation locus of the model. Moreover $\mathcal T$ is universal, in the sense that homeomorphic copies of it can be found densely in the activity loci of asymptotic values of any appropriate natural family of finite type meromorphic maps. When applied to the iterates of a transcendental meromorphic map, these results make it possible to build a transcendental renormalization theory, a question that has been open for the last 25 years.
item.dc:creator: Matthieu Astorg, Anna Miriam Benini, N\'uria Fagella

item.title: An upper bound on the growth of minimal graphs
item.description: arXiv:2604.19630v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Graphs of solutions to the minimal surface equation over simply connected domains with boundary values 0 can have at most exponential growth.
item.dc:creator: Allen Weitsman

item.title: Delta-pulse solution in Zener viscoelastic model
item.description: arXiv:2606.04024v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive an exact integral representation of the response to an impulsive boundary excitation in a semi-infinite, homogeneous, linear viscoelastic medium governed by the Zener model. Starting from the Bromwich integral, we analytically invert the relevant Laplace transforms and express the response in terms of modified Bessel functions of the first kind and Macdonald functions of half-integer order. The representation reduces to the known Maxwell solution in the appropriate limit. As an independent computational approach, we characterize the saddle points of the phase function and construct the associated steepest-descent path (SDP). Its branches satisfy a sixth-degree polynomial equation in the imaginary part of the complex variable, which is cubic in its square. Numerical comparisons for several model parameters confirm the agreement of the two methods. The integral representation reveals the structure of the response, whereas the SDP approach requires no closed-form inverse Laplace transform and can therefore be applied to more general viscoelastic models.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Mentrelli, Juan Luis Gonzalez-Santander, Francesco Mainardi

item.title: Sectorial normalisation of one resonant biholomorphisms near a fixed point
item.description: arXiv:2609.24695v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we study germs of biholomorphisms of $(\C^n,0)$, $n\geq 2$ fixing the origin, the linear part at which has all its eigenvalues on the unit circle. We prove the existence of a {\it sectorial} transformation to a polynomial normal form of a non-degenerate 1-resonant biholomorphism under a Diophantine condition. We also give their holomorphic classification. We show that the {\it sectorial} automorphisms of the polynomial normal form are {\it exponentially flat} perturbations of the identity. We deduce the Gevrey character of the formal normalizing transformation and we show how the Gevrey index depends on the Diophantine exponent.
item.dc:creator: Maxime Chatal (CNRS,UniCA), Laurent Stolovitch (CNRS,UniCA)

item.title: Algebraic properties of Truncated Toeplitz $+$ Truncated Hankel operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.35897v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the algebraic properties of $\mathcal{S}_\theta$ --- the class of truncated Toeplitz plus truncated Hankel operators --- on the model space $\mathcal{K}_\theta$. We also give a complete characterization of the intersection class of truncated Toeplitz and truncated Hankel operators. As a by-product of our findings, we give a complete characterization for $S_\theta$, where $\theta$ is a finite Blaschke product and also obtained the commutant of $S_\theta + S_\theta^{*}$ in that case.
item.dc:creator: Kritika Babbar, Satyabrata Majee, Amit Maji

item.title: Canonical Projectivization of Algebraic Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.04314v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct canonical projective birational models of normal proper integral algebraic spaces over arbitrary fields. The construction preserves the intrinsic quasi-projective core and is natural under semilinear isomorphisms. For smooth proper integral input in characteristic zero, we combine an intrinsic choice of ideals with W{\l}odarczyk's principalization to obtain a canonical tower of blowups in smooth centers ending in a smooth projective variety. Consequently, every compact connected Moishezon manifold admits a smooth projective bimeromorphic model to which all automorphisms lift compatibly. The main ingredient is a family-sum argument yielding an intrinsic finite selection of maximal tuples of boundary ideal germs; successive modifications strictly decrease the boundary-image dimension. We also construct canonical quasi-projective models for nonproper normal input and a greatest schematizing ideal for separated finite-type algebraic spaces over noetherian bases. Oda's threefold illustrates the construction.
item.dc:creator: Parsa Bakhtary
